summary: This is a closed GitHub issue (#158) from the gofiber/fiber repository titled 'How do I Set/Get data in context?', opened by hyingreborn on February 20, 2020. The user wants to pass JWT claims from middleware to a route handler, and maintainer Fenny answered that the Locals method should be used. Later commenters asked how Locals can take two parameters, and sixcolors explained that the method takes a key and an optional value, acting as a getter or setter.
one_line: GitHub issue in gofiber/fiber asking how to pass data from middleware to a route handler, answered by using Ctx Locals.
key_facts: The GitHub issue is #158 in the gofiber/fiber repository, titled 'How do I Set/Get data in context?'.
The issue was opened by hyingreborn on February 20, 2020 and was closed as completed by Fenny on the same day.
hyingreborn wanted to save user information in JWT middleware and retrieve it in the routing handler.
Fenny, a Member of the project, answered that the project uses Locals and linked to the documentation.
Fenny's example calls c.Locals("claims", claims) in app.Use("/api", ...) and claims := c.Locals("claims") in the GET handler for /api/v1/manager.
The issue was labeled 'question' and then 'solved'.
On February 20, 2024, martirosharutyunyan asked how c.Locals can accept two parameters.
sixcolors, a Member, replied that Locals takes a key and an optional value, acting as a getter when the value is omitted and a setter when it is provided.

sixcolors quoted the implementation: func (c *DefaultCtx) Locals(key any, value ...any) any, which calls c.fasthttp.UserValue(key) when no value is given and c.fasthttp.SetUserValue(key, value[0]) otherwise.
On September 21, 2022, acidjazz said Locals is an awesome feature and suggested it be listed elsewhere so users can find it more easily.
ReneWerner87 linked the Fiber documentation page at docs.gofiber.io/api/ctx#locals on September 21, 2022.
levniko, a newcomer to Fiber, asked on August 6, 2022 how to reach the claims value set with Locals in the handler.
The thread shows 8 participants, and the issue has 7 comments according to its header.
